idiom_name: interface State + classes implementing it + context field
implementation_notes: The TypeScript version of the classic structure: an interface (or abstract class when states share behaviour), one class per state, and a context with a state field it delegates through; the implements clause checks at compile time that each state provides the operations, while the runtime remains ordinary prototype delegation. This is the right shape when states hold injected dependencies, need identity shared across contexts, or when the codebase already organises behaviour in services. Structural typing means any matching object literal is accepted, so keep constructors and the state field non-public where the graph must not be bypassed.
pitfalls: Structural typing accepts any object with a matching shape, so an accidental literal can become a state; keep state constructors behind a factory or module boundary.
The interface is erased at runtime, so serialized or logged state needs an explicit discriminant - class names are minified away.
States that need services must receive them; instantiating services inside state classes hard-codes the graph and hurts testability.

variants.name: Discriminated union with an exhaustive switch
variants.idiom_name: type Phase = { kind: 'draft' } | { kind: 'published'; version: number } + switch on kind
variants.implementation_notes: The union encoding is the usual preference in typed codebases: states become a discriminated union, transitions produce new values, and switching on the discriminant narrows each state so payloads are reachable only in the right branch; an assertNever helper turns a forgotten state into a compile error, which is what buys exhaustiveness that TypeScript does not check by itself. Prefer it when the graph is data - serializable, testable, renderable - and the context holds no per-state dependencies; keep classes when states are behavioural objects with collaborators.
pitfalls: Without the assertNever arm the switch is silently non-exhaustive - the helper is the only thing enforcing completeness.
Narrowing only works on the discriminant, so comparing whole objects or strings defeats it.
Union values are erased at runtime: validate external data before treating it as a Phase, otherwise a malformed payload reaches the switch.
